metadata.selection_criteria: API-managed, generalist, demonstrated traction, no fees (see Marketplace Selection Criteria)

findings.title: v2: Criteria Applied Rigorously
findings.summary: Original bootstrap list was aspirational. This version applies the four hard criteria. Only 5 of 14 evaluated platforms pass or conditionally pass.
findings.details:
PASS (dataset marketplaces):
  Azure Marketplace         3% fee, full Partner Center API, massive buyer base
  Databricks Marketplace    0% fee, full REST/SDK/CLI API (confirmed)

PASS (API marketplaces):
  RapidAPI                  20–25% fee, 4M+ devs, largest API marketplace globally
  APILayer                  15% fee, curated quality, moderate traction

CONDITIONAL PASS:
  Dewey Data                No API, but they manage everything for you

FAIL (9 platforms):
  Datarade       → No API without Monda ($6K+/yr subscription)
  Nomad Data     → No API (email-only lead-gen), thin traction
  Opendatabay    → No API (uploads still in development), 1-person company
  Data & Sons    → Traction unverifiable
  Monda          → $6K+/yr subscription fee
  Nasdaq DL      → Finance-only (not generalist)
  Eagle Alpha    → No API (human introductions)
  Neudata        → No API (human introductions)
  Defined.ai     → AI training data only (not generalist)

findings.title: Azure Marketplace — NEW ADDITION
findings.summary: Full Partner Center API, 3% flat fee, 58,000+ products, massive enterprise buyer base. Integrated with Azure consumption commitments (MACC drawdown).
findings.details:
API: Partner Center APIs + SaaS Fulfillment APIs v2. Programmatic offer creation, listing management, billing.
GENERALIST: Yes — 58,000+ products across all categories.
TRACTION: Massive — enterprise buyers across every sector.
FEES: 3% flat store service fee. No upfront listing fees.
APPROVAL: Must join Microsoft Partner Network (free tier available).
DELIVERY: SaaS with API delivery, or Azure Data Share for dataset access.

Was excluded from original primary list as "fragmented, smaller data catalog" vs AWS/Snowflake. But it passes all 4 criteria and has massive buyer reach. Belongs in our distribution strategy.

findings.title: Databricks Marketplace — UPGRADED from "investigate"
findings.summary: Full programmatic API confirmed: REST API, Python SDK, CLI. Full CRUD for listings, files, exchanges, provider profiles. 0% fee.
findings.details:
API CONFIRMED:
  REST: /api/2.0/marketplace-provider/listings (create, get, list, update, delete)
  SDK:  w.provider_listings.create(), .update(), .delete() (databricks-sdk Python)
  CLI:  databricks provider-listings create --json '...'

Also covers: provider files (icons, notebooks), exchanges, provider profiles, analytics dashboards.
Delta Sharing shares fully managed via Unity Catalog API.

Full automation pipeline:
  Terraform → Unity Catalog + schemas + tables
  Pipeline  → ETL populates tables
  SDK       → CREATE SHARE + ADD TABLE
  SDK       → provider_files.create() (icon, notebooks)
  SDK       → provider_listings.create() (listing ref share)
  Monitor   → system.marketplace.listing_funnel_events

findings.title: RapidAPI — API Delivery Channel
findings.summary: Largest API marketplace globally. 4M+ developers, 175 countries, 35,000+ APIs. 20–25% commission. Best for data-as-API products.
findings.details:
API: Full provider tooling — documentation generation, tiered pricing plans, billing automation, key management, analytics.
GENERALIST: Yes — 30+ categories.
TRACTION: Very strong — billions of API calls/month. Acquired by Nokia (Nov 2024).
FEES: 20–25% commission. No upfront costs.
PAYOUT: PayPal only.

STRATEGIC FIT: If we build data products with API access (aligns with "agent-ready distribution" thesis), RapidAPI gives 4M+ developer reach at zero upfront cost. We'd need an API layer, but we're likely building that anyway.

CAVEATS: Nokia acquisition could change terms. High commission. PayPal-only payouts.

findings.title: APILayer — API Delivery Channel
findings.summary: Curated API marketplace. 75+ APIs, 15% commission, lower than RapidAPI. Providers must host on approved cloud platforms. Monthly payouts.
findings.details:
API: Providers host their own APIs; APILayer handles key management, payment collection, customer acquisition.
GENERALIST: Yes — AI/ML, finance, geolocation, and more.
TRACTION: Moderate — curated (quality over quantity). Active developer community. Established since 2022.
FEES: 15% commission. No upfront costs. Monthly payouts.
HOSTING: Must host on AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean, Scaleway, or Hetzner.

Lower commission than RapidAPI (15% vs 20–25%) but smaller audience. Curation means they may reject submissions — could work in our favour once listed.

findings.title: Dewey Data — CONDITIONAL PASS
findings.summary: No API, but white-glove managed service: they handle listing creation, sales, delivery, contracts, support, compliance. Provider sets up one data feed (~30 min) and that's it.
findings.details:
API: None. All APIs (Python, R, CLI) are consumer-facing only.
WHY CONDITIONAL: Dewey absorbs all operational friction. Provider responsibilities:
  • One-time: set up data feed (S3/Snowflake/SFTP) ~30 min
  • Ongoing: keep producing data into same feed location
  • That's it. Dewey does the rest.

DEWEY HANDLES: listing creation, metadata, sales, delivery, contracts, researcher support, compliance, reporting, citation tracking.
GENERALIST: Yes — real estate, mobility, labor, consumer, corporate, government, financial, weather, tech.
TRACTION: ~30 providers, MIT/Stanford/NYU/Berkeley as buyers.
FEES: Revenue share only (% undisclosed).
SMALL PROVIDERS: LobbyingData.com (single founder), NatureQuant, Capology.

LIMITATION: Schema changes require manual coordination. No self-service control. Academic buyers = lower revenue per sale.

Meets the spirit of criterion 1 (zero friction) but not the letter (no API).

findings.title: Failed Platforms — Evidence
findings.summary: 9 platforms evaluated and rejected with specific evidence for each failure.
findings.details:
DATARADE — No provider API. Must use Monda ($6K+/yr subscription + 20–30% commission) for any programmatic access. Monda API undocumented, Professional tier only.

NOMAD DATA — No API. Email-based lead-gen only. $4.8M funding over 5+ years, ~7 employees, no Series A. No independent reviews. "4,900 providers" is inflated (free frictionless signup).

OPENDATABAY — No API. Upload features still "being developed" (per their docs). 1 FTE + 13 volunteers, no funding. 46 providers, 327 datasets. Overdue company accounts at UK Companies House. 17 GitHub stars total.

DATA & SONS — No independent reviews, no verifiable buyer metrics, no press coverage. Cannot confirm real transactions.

MONDA — ~$6K+/yr subscription (annual commitment). API only on Professional tier. No public API docs. Does not integrate with AWS Data Exchange.

NASDAQ DATA LINK — Finance/investment only. ~250 premium datasets. Not generalist.

EAGLE ALPHA / NEUDATA — Human introduction models. No listing management API. Fundamentally incompatible with automation.

DEFINED.AI — AI training data only (speech, text, image, video). Not general-purpose business data.

findings.title: Key Insight: The Bootstrap Gap
findings.summary: There is no rich ecosystem of small, easy-entry, API-managed data marketplaces. The landscape is sharply bifurcated: big cloud platforms (API, traction, but need approval) vs small platforms (low barrier, but portal-based and low traction).
findings.details:
The bootstrap strategy therefore shifts from "build credibility on small platforms first" to:

1. APPLY TO EVERYTHING IN PARALLEL — approval timelines are undefined, start early
2. USE NARRATIVE.IO AS EASIEST ON-RAMP — self-service, API-managed, no approval gate
3. USE DEWEY FOR ACADEMIC CREDIBILITY — they do all the work, small provider precedent
4. BUILD API DELIVERY FOR RAPIDAPI/APILAYER — different channel, zero approval friction
5. DON'T WAIT FOR BOOTSTRAP CREDIBILITY — just apply and see who approves first

findings.title: Revised Recommended Sequence
findings.summary: Updated rollout plan based on what actually passes the criteria.
findings.details:
IMMEDIATE (zero cost)
  Narrative.io        Self-service, no approval gate, API-managed
  Dewey Data          Submit partnership form (they do all the work)

MONTH 1–2 (cloud marketplaces — apply in parallel)
  AWS Data Exchange   Submit qualification request
  Snowflake           Create provider profile, begin paid listing vetting
  Databricks          Apply to Data Partner Program
  Google Analytics Hub  Enable API, create exchange (free listings first)
  Azure Marketplace   Join Microsoft Partner Network, submit listing

MONTH 2–3 (API marketplaces — if building API delivery)
  RapidAPI            List data APIs (20–25% commission, 4M+ devs)
  APILayer            List data APIs (15% commission, curated)

ONGOING
  Re-evaluate Datarade if they launch a free provider API
  Monitor Monda pricing for commission-only tier
  Watch for new marketplaces meeting all 4 criteria
